source_text.body:
Hand off repeat content and inbox chores to a bot
Commenters describe Grok Bot drafting and scheduling posts from transcripts, updating a meal-prep inventory from a fridge camera, and collecting replies into a Notion inbox with drafted responses.
·
Nov 17, 2026
Done with
GB
Grok Bot
What they did
In the thread, people describe giving Grok Bot access to routine workstreams rather than one-off prompts. Examples include feeding it transcripts so it can draft and schedule posts, connecting a fridge camera so it updates a meal-prep inventory list automatically, and wiring email and messaging into a bot that gathers replies into a Notion-style inbox and prewrites threaded responses for a person to edit and send.
How it went
The reported payoff was less manual checking and drafting: one manager said email triage dropped from about two hours a day to under 10 messages left in the inbox, while others said they stopped guessing what food was left or writing routine replies from scratch. The thread is anecdotal, so commenters share wins but give little hard detail on failure rates.
Worth knowing
The clearest catch is setup: commenters describe connecting accounts and teaching the bot their workflow over time, then stepping in mainly to review or tweak drafts.
Try it yourself
with
Grok Bot
Copy prompt
Take over these recurring chores for me: turn each new transcript in [folder or link] into [number] draft posts for [platform] in my voice and queue them for my approval, and collect replies from [email or inbox] into a Notion page called [page name] with a drafted response for each. Do this every [frequency]. Never publish a post or send a reply until I approve it, and send me a short summary after each run.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/GrokBot/comments/1xxhyk8/megathread_what_have_you_stopped_doing_manually
